reason: The target is a commencement provision and note, not an ongoing study rule.
The opening section separates core definitions from rules about when a claim is brought and what counts as a limitation period under the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Claim, claimant, and defendant definitions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 1(1) defines the central persons and claim concept used throughout the limitation regime.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify claim, claimant, and defendant under the Act.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: When a claim is brought and limitation-period references
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 1(2) and 1(3) specify when a claim is brought and exclude the section 22 period from references to limitation periods established by the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when a claim is brought and how limitation-period references exclude section 22.

reason: Focused application rule for claims brought after commencement, including added claims in older proceedings.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application of the Limitation of Actions Act
proposedGroups.reason: The operative subsection states the Act applies to claims brought after commencement, including claims added to pre-commencement proceedings.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State which claims the Limitation of Actions Act applies to.

reason: Single binding rule stating the Act binds the Crown.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown bound by the Limitation of Actions Act
proposedGroups.reason: The section contains only the Crown-binding rule.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State whether the Limitation of Actions Act binds the Crown.

reason: Conflict rule distinguishing public Act conflicts from private Act conflicts.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Conflict rules for public and private Acts
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections say other public Acts prevail over this Act, while this Act prevails over conflicting private Acts.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain which Act prevails when the Limitation of Actions Act conflicts with public or private Acts.

reason: Core limitation-period rule combining a two-year discovery period and fifteen-year ultimate period with a discovery test.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: General limitation periods and discovery of claims
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections state the earlier of two years from discovery and fifteen years from the act or omission, and define discovery by knowledge of injury, causation, and defendant act or omission.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the general limitation periods and when a claim is discovered.

reason: Single rule deeming a continuous act or omission to occur separately each day for section 5 limitation calculations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuous act or omission limitation calculation

evidenceText: deemed for the purposes of calculating the limitation periods
a separate act or omission on each day it continues

proposedGroups.reason: The text tells how continuous conduct is treated when calculating section 5 limitation periods.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State how continuous acts or omissions are treated for limitation-period calculations.

reason: Single application rule excluding Part 2 from Part 3 claims unless Part 3 provides otherwise.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application of Part 2 to Part 3 claims

evidenceText: Part 2 does not apply to the claims referred to in this Part

proposedGroups.reason: The text defines the default relationship between Part 2 and claims listed in the Part.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State the default application of Part 2 to claims referred to in this Part.

reason: Focused limitation rule for Crown money-recovery claims, including contract and tort damages claims.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Limitation periods for Crown recovery of money claims
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections apply Part 2 to Crown money claims and set the earlier of six years from discovery and fifteen years from the act or omission.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the limitation periods for Crown claims to recover money.

reason: Transitional limitation rule for Crown money claims based on acts or omissions before commencement of section 7.2.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Transition rules for Crown money-recovery limitation periods
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections define covered Crown claims and adjust limitation expiry to July 1, 2022 for specified pre-commencement periods.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how section 7.2 transitions Crown money-recovery limitation periods.

reason: Single fifteen-year limitation period for claims based on judgments for payment of money.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Limitation period for judgment payment claims

evidenceText: No claim based on a judgment for the payment of money
after 15 years from the day of the judgment

proposedGroups.reason: The text sets the limitation period for judgment-payment claims.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State the limitation period for a claim based on a judgment for payment of money.

reason: Recovery of land has distinct definition, base dispossession period, special present-interest or lease timing, dispossession rules, and extinguishment effect.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Lease, predecessor, and present interest definitions for land recovery
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 8.1(1) defines terms used in the land recovery limitation rules.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the defined terms used in section 8.1 recovery-of-land rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Base limitation periods for recovery of land
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 8.1(2) bars recovery after continuous dispossession for fifteen years, or sixty years if the claimant is the Crown.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State the base dispossession periods for claims to recover possession of land.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Present interest and fixed-term lease recovery timing
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 8.1(3) and 8.1(4) provide later deadlines where dispossession begins during a present interest or fixed-term lease.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how present interests and fixed-term leases extend land recovery timing.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Dispossession rules and extinguishment of land title
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 8.1(5) and 8.1(6) define when landlord and co-owner dispossession begins and extinguish right or title when the period expires.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize when dispossession begins for leases or co-owners and what expiry does to title.

reason: Focused limitation and title-extinguishment rule for converted personal property.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recovery of converted personal property and extinguishment of title
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections set different deadlines for good-faith value purchasers and other cases, and extinguish claimant title when the period expires.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the limitation periods for recovering converted personal property and the effect of expiry.

reason: Conversion damages rule applying Part 2 subject to a multiple-conversion bar tied to section 9 possession recovery.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Limitation rule for damages for conversion
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections apply Part 2 to conversion damages and bar claims after multiple conversions if section 9 possession recovery against that defendant is unavailable.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain when damages claims for conversion are governed by Part 2 or barred by section 9.

reason: Single limitation rule for failure to repay a demand loan.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Limitation period for demand loan repayment claims

evidenceText: failure to repay a demand loan
two years from the day default in repayment occurs
fifteen years from the day on which the lender is first entitled to make a demand

proposedGroups.reason: The text sets the earlier of the post-demand default period and ultimate demand-entitlement period.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State the limitation period for claims based on failure to repay a demand loan.

reason: Secured debt includes separate rules for Part 2 application, principal recovery, part payments, and redemption claims.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Claims for payment or principal of secured debt
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 12(1) and 12(2) apply Part 2 subject to a fifteen-year limit on principal recovery from when security is taken.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the limitation rule for claims to recover principal of secured debt.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Part payments and redemption claims for secured debt
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 12(3) and 12(4) treat payments as part payments of principal and interest and set a fifteen-year period for debtor redemption after creditor possession.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how secured-debt payments and creditor possession affect limitation periods.

reason: Single fifteen-year limitation period for recovering amounts due under statutory liens or charges.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Limitation period for statutory liens or charges

evidenceText: If a lien or charge is created by an Act
no claim shall be brought to recover the amount due after 15 years

proposedGroups.reason: The text sets the recovery deadline from the day the lien or charge arises.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: State the limitation period for recovering amounts due under a statutory lien or charge.

reason: Contribution has a general settlement or judgment limitation rule and a separate Tortfeasors Act contribution rule.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: General limitation periods for contribution claims
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 14(1) sets the earlier of two years from knowledge of contribution liability and the later of fifteen years from the underlying act or five years from payment, settlement, or judgment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the limitation periods for general contribution claims after payment, settlement, or judgment.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Tortfeasors Act contribution limitation period
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 14(2) gives a separate rule for contribution under paragraph 2(c) of the Tortfeasors Act, based on knowledge after settlement or pleading service and a fifteen-year ultimate period.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain the limitation period for Tortfeasors Act contribution claims.
